prompt: A new terminal answers `gcloud storage buckets list` with "You do not currently have an active account selected". What is the fix in this course?
hint: Which lines did that terminal never receive?

choices.text: Run gcloud auth login
choices.why: That is the advice for somebody with an account; here there is no account to log in to.

choices.text: Type the eight export lines in that terminal
choices.why: Right. The variables live in one terminal; without them gcloud looks for a login.

choices.text: Restart the gcs container, which has stopped
choices.why: A stopped emulator gives Connection refused on its port, not a missing account.

choices.text: Reinstall gcloud 591.0.0
choices.why: gcloud answered, so it is installed; it only lacked the variables.

prompt: You stopped both emulators last night and started them again this morning. What is left of yesterday's buckets and topics?
hint: Where do they keep what they are told?

choices.text: The buckets, which fake-gcs-server writes to disk
choices.why: It was started with -backend memory, so it writes nothing to disk.

choices.text: Both, kept in ~/gcp/venv
choices.why: The virtual environment holds Python packages, not anything an emulator was told.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right. Both keep everything in memory, and the containers were started with --rm.

choices.text: The topics, which Google's emulator keeps in the project planner-dev
choices.why: planner-dev is a name the emulator accepts, not a place that stores anything.

prompt: `terraform plan` prints a monitoring alert policy with no error, on your computer. What does that prove?
hint: Who computed the plan, and who was asked?

choices.text: That Google would accept the policy
choices.why: Nobody at Google was asked; the plan is computed locally by the provider.

choices.text: That the configuration is well formed for the provider
choices.why: Right. The provider knows every argument; whether Google accepts it, or what it costs, is unknown.

choices.text: That the alert will fire when the metric crosses its threshold
choices.why: Nothing evaluates an alert on your computer; that is taught from the documentation.

choices.text: That your account may create it
choices.why: There is no account, and no IAM answers locally.

prompt: Which of these happen for real on your computer in this course? Choose all that apply.
hint: Containers, emulators and local programs, yes; Google's control plane, no.

choices.text: A build step's container running the tests
choices.why: Yes. A step is a container, and Docker runs it.

choices.text: A message published to a Pub/Sub topic and received
choices.why: Yes. Google's Pub/Sub emulator answers on port 8085.

choices.text: A Cloud Build trigger firing on a push
choices.why: No. Nothing imitates Cloud Build; triggers are read from the documentation.

choices.text: Cloud Armor blocking a request
choices.why: No. No emulator enforces a security policy.

choices.text: Terraform's state written to a bucket and locked
choices.why: Yes. The gcs backend works against fake-gcs-server, lock included.

prompt: Where does every price in this course come from?

choices.text: From the emulators' billing endpoint
choices.why: The emulators have no billing at all.

choices.text: From an estimate the course made from similar services elsewhere
choices.why: No estimate is invented; each price is read from a page with its date.

choices.text: Google's public pricing pages, dated
choices.why: Right. A list price on a date, with no discount, credit or tax in it.

choices.text: From the bill of a real project
choices.why: There is no real project in this course.

prompt: The first step of a build runs `pip install requests` in the Python image. The second step, in the same image, imports `requests` and fails. Why?
hint: What passes from one step to the next?

choices.text: Each step starts from its own image; only /workspace is shared
choices.why: Right. The package went into the first container's site-packages, which died with it.

choices.text: pip needs the network, which steps do not have
choices.why: Steps do have the network; the install worked, in a container that then ended.

choices.text: The steps ran in parallel, so the install had not finished yet when the import ran
choices.why: Steps run in order unless waitFor says otherwise, and the second started after the first exited.

choices.text: The second step needs dir: api to find the package
choices.why: dir changes the starting directory, not where Python looks for installed packages.

prompt: What makes Cloud Build stop a build after a step?
hint: The tests' result reaches Cloud Build in one number.

choices.text: The word FAILED in the step's output
choices.why: Cloud Build does not read the output; a step printing FAILED and exiting 0 passes.

choices.text: A test report written to /workspace
choices.why: Files in /workspace are for later steps; they decide nothing.

choices.text: A step that writes anything to standard error, which Cloud Build treats as a failure
choices.why: Many tools write progress to standard error; it is not a failure.

choices.text: An exit status other than 0
choices.why: Right. That is the only gate a build has.

prompt: A step builds the image `southamerica-east1-docker.pkg.dev/planner-dev/shop/api:abc1234`, every step succeeds, and the image is not in the registry afterwards. What is the likeliest cause?
hint: What does Cloud Build do once every step has succeeded?

choices.text: The build's service account lacks the logging option
choices.why: Without it the build is refused before any step runs, so no step would have succeeded.

choices.text: The image is not in the build file's images list
choices.why: Right. An image nobody lists is thrown away with the machine.

choices.text: The tag abc1234 is too short for the registry
choices.why: Seven characters is exactly what $SHORT_SHA produces, and the registry accepts it.

choices.text: Docker images cannot be built inside a step
choices.why: The cloud-builders/docker image exists for exactly that, with the machine's daemon.

prompt: A trigger has `includedFiles: ["docs/**"]` by mistake, where `api/**` was meant. A developer merges a change to `api/app.py`. What happens?
hint: Which paths did the commit change, and which does the trigger watch?

choices.text: The build runs, because main always builds
choices.why: The branch matched, but the paths did not, and both must match.

choices.text: Nothing builds, and nothing reports it
choices.why: Right. That is the expensive failure: silence, not an error.

choices.text: Cloud Build rejects the trigger when it is created
choices.why: docs/** is a valid glob; nothing tells Cloud Build it is the wrong one.

choices.text: The build fails with an error naming the path
choices.why: No build starts, so there is no build to fail.

prompt: A step's args are `["-c", "echo $HOME"]`. What does Cloud Build do with it?
hint: Who sees the dollar sign first, the shell or Cloud Build?

choices.text: Prints the home directory of the step's user
choices.why: That needs $$HOME, so that the shell receives $HOME.

choices.text: Prints an empty line
choices.why: Cloud Build does not silently replace an unknown substitution with nothing.

choices.text: Refuses the build: HOME is not a substitution it knows
choices.why: Right. Unknown substitutions are an error unless ALLOW_LOOSE is set.

choices.text: Prints the literal text $HOME
choices.why: Cloud Build reads the dollar sign as a substitution before the shell sees it.

prompt: A pull request trigger builds every pull request, including from forks, with no comment required. Why is that a risk?
hint: Whose code runs, and as whom?

choices.text: The build minutes of forks are billed twice
choices.why: Minutes are billed once; the risk is what the code can do.

choices.text: A fork cannot read the substitutions
choices.why: Substitutions are filled in either way; that is not the danger.

choices.text: Builds from forks always fail, wasting a run
choices.why: They succeed perfectly well, which is the problem.

choices.text: A stranger's code runs as the build's service account
choices.why: Right. Requiring /gcbrun from a collaborator is the line between running tests and running anything.

prompt: A user-defined substitution, such as the one naming the shop's region, begins with an ___.
The shop's image builds in 40 seconds on a laptop and in 4 minutes on Cloud Build. What is the likeliest reason?
hint: What did the laptop have from the build before?

choices.text: Cloud Build starts with no layer cache
choices.why: Right. Every build is a fresh machine, so every instruction runs again.

choices.text: Cloud Build machines are slower than any laptop
choices.why: The default machine is comparable; the work it does is what differs.

choices.text: The time spent waiting in the queue is counted as part of the build
choices.why: Queue time is neither built nor billed; the build itself is slower.

choices.text: Cloud Build compresses every layer twice before pushing it
choices.why: Nothing like that happens; the missing cache is the difference.

prompt: A Dockerfile copies the whole repository, then runs `pip install -r requirements.txt`, then sets the command. Which change helps every build after a code-only commit, with or without a cache in the registry?
hint: Which layer changes when only the code changes?

choices.text: Switching the build to e2-highcpu-32
choices.why: A bigger machine runs the same install faster and costs ten times more a minute; the install still runs.

choices.text: Copying requirements.txt and installing before copying the code
choices.why: Right. A code change then leaves the install layer untouched and reusable.

choices.text: Adding --no-cache to the build
choices.why: That forbids reusing any layer, the opposite of what is wanted.

choices.text: Moving pip install to its own step in cloudbuild.yaml
choices.why: A step's installs vanish with its container; the image would not have the packages.

prompt: A build runs 8 minutes on e2-standard-2 at 0.006 USD a minute, 560 times in a month. What does the month cost after the 2,500 free build minutes?
hint: Total minutes, less 2,500, times the price.

prompt: Put what happens to the shop's code, from a merge to `main` until the image is in the registry, in order.
hint: The trigger reads the file before anything runs.
items: The trigger matches the branch and the changed paths
Cloud Build fills in the substitutions
The test step runs in the Python image
The build step builds the image
The image in the images list is pushed
trap: Pushing before the tests is the slip: images is pushed only once every step has succeeded.
